content: The R. Anjām (also titled Taṣavvuf va Ḥurūf), written in or before 828/1425, compares Sufism and lettrism. It first sets Sufism beside philosophy, both quests for wisdom (ḥikmat) and noble sciences within their own ambit, but says neither can compete with lettrism, presented as the supreme science of the age; it is written in the most accessible manner possible to promote the science.
